Cities destroyed, laws vanished, and monsters roamed freely as humanity struggled to survive in a reality ruled by game-like system with levels, power, and brutal evolution.

But his fate changed when five women from another world reached out to him. Each of them bound by their own goals, secrets, and reasons for helping him.
Through intimate contracts that transcended flesh and soul, they shared power with him, pushing his growth far beyond ordinary limits.

His solution? Sell. His father's? A lecture about the club's “soul.”

He’s done trying to fix the past; he's going to build the future.
Liquidating his lavish lifestyle, he gambles everything he has on a radical experiment: to create a football club run purely by logic.
He'll scout with algorithms, sign players based on statistical value, and manage with cold, calculated strategy. He’s building a machine designed for one purpose: to dominate.

He drifted through time, witnessing the world of football from the perspective of a ghost. It was strange, unpleasant, yet exciting. No need for tickets or travel—he could simply fly.
England, Italy, Spain, Germany—the best football countries in Europe—and even the passionate South America, the energetic Africa, and the growing Asia—Richard observed the rise and fall of football giants, all from the sidelines.
However, watching football from the other side was quite different from experiencing it live. He missed the cheering, singing, and chanting with the other fans. No one could hear him now. No one could watch football with him. He was... alone.

Do you believe in reincarnation?
Some people would say yes, while others would say no.
But what if it truly existed? Surely, everyone—especially those who felt like failures in life—would wish for another chance to live, right?
***
Merlin Ken, a renowned editor, died while reviewing the raw draft of a popular novel titled “The Lost Hero.”
But instead of moving on to the afterlife, he awoke to find himself reincarnated inside the very novel he had been editing!

25th century prodigy Xiao Wushuang was betrayed and killed by her boyfriend and sister, but woke up again to find herself reincarnated as a farmgirl and equipped with a spatial pocket with a luck stat. The Peng Society for Gentlemen — a secret friend-making club for the homosexual men of the Great Xia Dynasty. Its services were designed to help its members along in their quest for their lifelong partners. Upon paying a monthly fee of fifty coins, members could get themselves listed in The Pengornisseur after providing a self-portrait, a mailing address, their age and hobbies, as well as a self-introduction. All members would receive a copy of the monthly publication, and they could communicate with one another in private using the information in The Pengornisseur.
Wu Xingzi, a bachelor about to turn forty, worked as the adviser to the magistrate in Qingcheng County.
Qingcheng County was a place with barely any resources. In other words, it was poor. In the list of counties of the Great Xia Dynasty, it had been ranked at the bottom for the past two hundred years.
Wu Xingzi felt that his life was hopeless: not only was he a homosexual, he was also a virgin. Even his retirement fund was lacking. Worse still, his looks were… forgettable.
He might as well die.
Hence, Wu Xingzi decided to commit suicide on his fortieth birthday.…
